notes.title: Stellar Insurgency - DEMO v4.3 and more
notes.content: [p][b]Welcome to another update for Stellar Insurgency![/b][/p][p][b]Stellar Insurgency - DEMO v4.3 and more.[/b][/p][h3][b]Trading – Trade Routes & Colony Types[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Star systems are linked by trade routes that form the backbone of interstellar commerce. Trading follows a supply and demand system, where commodities move along these routes to meet the needs of colonies. Trade routes can be disrupted if cargo ships traveling them are destroyed, creating shortages and destabilizing local economies. Beyond established routes, goods can also be exchanged through wandering traders—or acquired through pirates.[/p][p]Each colony has a type and a size, which together determine its production, consumption, and strategic value.[/p][p][b]Colony Types[/b][/p][list][*][p]Mining Colony[/p][/*][*][p]Agricultural World[/p][/*][*][p]Industrial Hub[/p][/*][*][p]Trade Hub[/p][/*][*][p]Core World[/p][/*][*][p]Military Base[/p][/*][*][p]Frontier Colony[/p][/*][*][p]Penal Colony[/p][/*][*][p]Smuggler's Outpost[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Colony Sizes[/b][/p][list][*][p]Outpost[/p][/*][*][p]Settlement[/p][/*][*][p]Colony[/p][/*][*][p]City-State[/p][/*][*][p]Planetary Metropolis[/p][/*][/list][p]Each colony type has unique production and consumption patterns that scale with its size. For example an Industrial Hub produces spare parts and components, but consumes raw materials and food. while a Core World produces supplies but consumes large amounts of food and spare parts.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/45aaf5befd7d5aef79b7b4a3cfd32c5f8c186573.jpg"][/img]Each colony type has distinct production and consumption patterns that scale with its size, displayed on the colony trading screen.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/48798bf8f04fc563e7584766d4fa1627e2dbd8d1.jpg"][/img]Galactic trade routes. Trade routes can be disrupted if cargo ships traveling them are destroyed, creating shortages and destabilizing local economies.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3][b]Crew Traits[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Every crew member has one or more traits, determined by their rank and role. For example a Commander might boost sensor range and reduce energy consumption of components. while a Security Officer might reduce shield restoration time. Traits from the fleet leader (player) and individual ship captains provide global bonuses to the rest of the crew. Crew members can level up from 1 to 10, with each level improving their traits by +1%. In addition crew members can be part of the away team during exploration with various benefits and penalties.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/e78a0c7213fc164989781d522d93665fff3e0573.jpg"][/img]Every crew member has one or more traits, determined by their rank and role.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Scanning – Normal vs. Deep[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Currently there are two Scan Modes.[/p][list][*][p]Normal Scan – Reveals cargo, crew, and passenger cabins.[/p][/*][*][p]Deep Scan – Reveals ship components.[/p][/*][/list][p]Normal scanning reveals a ship’s cargo bays, crew, and cabins, while deep scanning exposes its internal components. Deep scans should be used sparingly, as they negatively affect diplomatic relations between the scanning and scanned factions. The level of the installed scanner also plays a significant role in determining which components are revealed after deep scanning the object.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/969edbc2bebf59a41cc542218b8eaf2de08f2b2f.jpg"][/img]Deep scanning this ship. [/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/d7d15ed079e7aa17109cff64ad7ce75e75011aa2.jpg"][/img]We need to scan this object to uncover the contents of its cargo bay.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Hailing Colonies[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]The player can now hail colonies in addition to ships. Colonies respond dynamically based on their current state, providing useful information about conditions, resources, and potential opportunities.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/60c5f36d4bcc155a0cbdaf8d82de2b9bda4a3931.jpg"][/img]The player can now hail colonies in addition to ships.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]I’m currently focused on enhancing the game’s procedural systems, aiming to build a richly interconnected world where dynamic events foster emergent gameplay—ensuring that every playthrough is not only unique, but also truly distinct.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you for reading.[/p][p]Tensorial[/p]

notes.title: Demo v4, Galaxy update, Scanline Effect, Better Hail Screen, Log Panel and more
notes.content:
[b]DISCLAIMER: In this update I use AI generated images as a placeholder for avatars and landscapes.[/b]

Welcome to another major update for Stellar Insurgency!

Update Highlights
[list]
[*] Demo v4 Released
[*] Galaxy Improvements
[*] Scanline Effect for Communications Panel
[*] Enhanced Hail Screen
[*] Updated Landscape Images for Galaxy's objects.
[*] New Galaxy Log Panel (or Captain's Log :))
[*] Smoother Spaceship Stopping Animation
[/list]

[b]Demo v4 Released[/b]

Demo v4 is now available! It includes all previous updates and introduces the ability for players to travel to a neighboring solar system.

[b]Realistic Star Density Distribution[/b]

The star density distribution now aligns with the density patterns of a particle-simulated spiral galaxy.
This realistic approach is based on the Density Wave Model, ensuring that the galaxy's structure mirrors scientifically accurate principles. Accessible stars are distributed according to this density, making exploration feel more immersive and authentic. In the future, I plan to introduce customizable sliders on the start screen, enabling players to create their own spiral galaxy by adjusting parameters like star density, galaxy shape, and overall size.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/c4d4c72c44857ee14eccfe4c06c246ddca2fe4f1.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/d3ec873fa126e79b172e7362f1a80308b9c2d529.jpg[/img]

[b]Scanline Effect for Communications Panel[/b]

To enhance immersion, a scanline effect has been added to the main image of the communications panel. This subtle, yet impactful visual detail provides a retro-futuristic aesthetic, mimicking the feel of classic sci-fi interfaces. It also helps to visually separate the communications panel from other UI elements, reinforcing its importance as a primary channel for receiving and interpreting mission-critical information. The effect dynamically adjusts with the panel's lighting, ensuring a consistent and engaging user experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/3e8c788e88ceca561a47a3a6621995ff7ca5880a.jpg[/img]

[b]Enhanced Hail Screen[/b]

Each faction now has unique characters with distinctive avatars.
Faction-specific designs are reflected in their ships' bridge backgrounds, showcasing their characteristic style. When interacting with planetary colonies, players will also see different room environments for each faction, adding depth and variety to interactions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/932bfe1aab5344a12fe5953d1015d492c200a3cb.jpg[/img]

[b]Updated Landscape Images for Galaxy's objects.[/b]

The landscape images of all planetoids have been updated, further strengthening the procedural aspect of the game. Each image is now meticulously designed to match the descriptive features of the corresponding celestial object, from barren rocky terrains to lush alien vistas. This update bridges the gap between the visual and narrative elements of the game, allowing players to feel a stronger connection to the worlds they explore. The variety and uniqueness of the images emphasize the distinctiveness of each planetoid, enhancing the depth of the game's universe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/2d8ff0d397f635c8c24ccb2cc8cdb5f401ed5980.jpg[/img]

[b]New Galaxy Log Panel (or Captain's Log :))[/b]

A new log panel has been introduced to provide players with a centralized repository of relevant information about the galaxy and their actions. This panel serves as a comprehensive record, storing details about major events, player fleet configurations, and exploration reports. It offers an organized and accessible way for players to review their progress, analyze past decisions, and plan future strategies. By integrating this feature, the game ensures that players remain engaged with the evolving narrative and mechanics of the galaxy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/6f7b1362cd403efc8af7f74e28e7f0adda17881b.jpg[/img]

[b]Smoother Spaceship Stopping Animation[/b]

The animation for the spaceship's stopping sequence has been significantly refined to ensure smoother transitions. When the spaceship decelerates, the movement now feels fluid and natural, improving the overall visual quality. Additionally, the engines gradually power down in sync with the ship's motion,
with subtle visual and audio cues marking the shutdown. These enhancements not only improve the aesthetic appeal but also add a layer of realism, making the act of navigating and stopping the spaceship feel more immersive and polished.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/b3c0a17e1e78cf8b661444f528f12d94aa583043.gif[/img]

My goal is to create a richly procedural world with interconnected events, ensuring that every playthrough is not only unique but also feels truly distinct.

Have a happy new year!
Tensorial

notes.title: Stellar Insurgency - More Exploration
notes.content:
Welcome to another update for Stellar Insurgency!

In this post, I’ll discuss the new additions to the three-stage exploration system introduced in the previous dev diary.

Stage One: [b]Scanning[/b]
Stage Two: [b]Probing[/b]
Stage Three: [b]Away Team Exploration[/b]

To proceed to the second or third stages, players must first complete a scan of the target.

The three-stage exploration process has now been expanded to include not only planets but also spaceships and other objects within each solar system, adding new layers of depth and discovery.

Similarly, in the third exploration stage, players now have the option to board an enemy ship using a boarding probe or transporter—provided their fleet is equipped with one of these components and the enemy ship’s shields are lowered or inactive. Additionally, players can assign ranked crew members (such as a captain or commander) to the exploration team. These high-ranking crew members bring unique benefits, adding strategic depth and enhancing the team’s capabilities during missions.

Additionally, through the Interact button on a spaceship, players can now request available intel on an NPC spacecraft. The information displayed on the intel panel is dynamic, updating based on the player’s actions or changes in the NPC ship’s status, providing a more immersive and responsive experience.

Finally, I’ve expanded the variety of planets, with each one presenting unique dangers for the exploration team. These distinct planetary hazards add depth and challenge to each mission, making every exploration a unique experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/a5047c9f12fcf7d0777c065f0f073fd8da4fadb3.jpg[/img]
Before scanning, the contents of the enemy ship's cargo bays are hidden.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/b3dc1b31f9f1d4ee47b016a0c817ea8ac7ff702c.jpg[/img]
In this image, an NPC ship is being scanned using available sensors.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/502fceae3eb2e645a5c381b8442932e5100deedd.jpg[/img]
After scanning, the contents of the ship's cargo bays are revealed.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/325eeba2eb5fadaa98d5a5a1e73710151ba33e1e.jpg[/img]
After scanning, the crew composition of an NPC ship is now revealed. Furthermore, players can now assign one or more ranked crew members to the Away Team during the third exploration stage (using the toggle next to the crew image), providing unique benefits or exposing the team to potential penalties based on their choices.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/3403cc61fc1455f603f28951acb5bfd9d5032f09.jpg[/img]
Through the Interact button on a spaceship, players can now request available intel on an NPC spacecraft.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/c47ca11e9ba39d908612807b022760d3a1468d7c.jpg[/img]
The information displayed on the intel panel is dynamic, updating based on the player's actions or changes in the NPC ship's status, providing a more immersive and responsive experience.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/bf1c7e9da7c691ff4a1b62f05a5ef2ea1fda1409.jpg[/img]
Expanded the diversity of planets, each featuring its own unique dangers for the exploration team. These distinct hazards introduce depth and challenge to every mission, ensuring that no two explorations feel the same.

Thank you,

Tensorial

notes.title: Revamped research screen, Update on Exploration System and more
notes.content:
In this update, the tech tree and research screen have been revamped, and the exploration aspect of the game has been significantly enhanced, among other improvements.

The tech tree has been revamped and divided into five distinct categories in the Research screen.

[b]1. Fleet & Logistics[/b]
       Fleet Logistics
       Crew Efficiency
       Jump Drive Efficiency

[b]2. Propulsion & Navigation[/b]
       Engines
       Sensors
       Jump Inhibitor

[b]3. Support & Utility Systems[/b]
       Reactor
       Tractor Beam
       Exploration Techs
       Other, like universal translator

[b]4. Defensive Systems[/b]
       Point Defense
       Stealth Field
       Shields
       Armor

[b]5. Weapons Systems[/b]
       Laser Turrets
       Rail Turrets
       Missiles & Rockets
       Flak guns and small space-fighter guns

Currently, there are 84 technologies in the tech tree, with more planned for the future. The technologies are separated in efficiency technologies and component technologies. When a technology related to a spaceship component is researched, its blueprint appears in the blueprint tab of the fleet screen. The component can then be synthesized there, provided the required materials are available in the fleet's cargo bays. For the full tech tree, see the end of this article.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/0bb1c224bde506a5e70559bc68d0f67ef1fc3af8.jpg[/img]

Unresearched components can be purchased from markets or discovered through exploration and installed on the spaceship, but they cannot be synthesized. Only researched components can be synthesized and made available at the player’s demand. Making technologies available through markets, exploration, or other in-game events, rather than solely through a tech tree, can add depth, variety, and strategic elements to the game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/e45c5696266082bcc9e0a5719e1d4b06c7d1e401.jpg[/img]

The spaceship info frame has been updated to convey valuable information to the player more efficiently. The new version provides information about the ship's available energy, the jump state of the engines (time remaining before ready to jump), the status of the stealth system and force fields (shields), the damage state or availability of other important components of the ship or other objects, and more.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/f53fdf02b66a15c22389cc5f651349425984ecd2.jpg[/img]

The billboard shader has been updated to eliminate color saturation issues caused by the bloom effect when multiple spaceships are in close proximity.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/85b0e38d4004cfa644ad5ab77f137dfc4e7a3f75.jpg[/img]

[b]Update on Exploration System[/b]

I've focused on enhancing the exploration aspect of the game by upgrading the previous,
simplistic probe-based system to a more engaging, three-stage exploration process.

[b]Stage One: Scanning[/b]

Players can now scan a planet if they have a spaceship equipped with a Scanner device.
This initial scan provides basic information, such as the presence of mineral deposits (without revealing quantities) and other general details. Completing this stage is a prerequisite for advancing to the next two stages.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/13dc16468a4e9c3d34be76aec85d63d1c602dffd.jpg[/img]

[b]Stage Two: Probing[/b]

After scanning, players can deploy a probe if their spaceship is equipped with a probe launcher and has probes available in its cargo bay. Probing offers more detailed rewards, such as retrieving mineral samples, but also introduces potential risks, like the appearance of hostile entities.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/c409b95c74cfaf9cbba0e8d0cd72cc4e9ed0fa77.jpg[/img]

[b]Stage Three: Away Team Exploration[/b]

The final stage involves sending an away team to the planet, provided the player has a transporter and available crew. During this stage, a dialogue tree will appear, prompting the player to make decisions that guide the exploration process. The rewards are greater, but so are the dangers. Players might need to decide whether to take risks for potential gains or play it safe, knowing that the wrong choice could lead to crew casualties.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/3948817a62374897ca168019d9321433d26a0fcd.jpg[/img]

[b]Additional Improvements:[/b]

Dynamic Description Panel: The description panel has been significantly enhanced to display dynamic information that reflects the state of the game. For instance, it shows the current exploration stage and additional details based on player choices and the overall condition of the solar system or galaxy.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/5fdeba27dcc4bbfcaaa8fd802d62aa48e38b415b.jpg[/img]

Enhanced Dialogue System: The rudimentary dialogue system has been replaced with a more robust dialogue tree (or graph), and I've exposed all necessary functionalities in the editor to support modding. This makes it easier for players or modders to create and customize their own conversation scenarios.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/d2c3b63f8e87529c004f67eb7568bf065a94554f.jpg[/img]

Thank you,
Tensorial

notes.title: Tech Tree
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/02ae7449e0bede76afe5c2de22e5cad84d5207dd.png[/img]

Researching technology takes time (as indicated by the number of days next to the tech's name) and requires a tech officer to begin. If multiple officers are assigned, research progresses faster.

Most technologies are self-explanatory and include fleet, engine, sensor, defense, and weapon upgrades.

When a technology that unlocks a component (e.g., a weapon) is researched, its blueprint becomes available in the fleet screen, where it can be synthesized if the necessary raw materials are in the fleet's cargo bays.

Researching efficiency technologies offers various benefits. For example, 'Engineer Efficiency' allows fleet engines to be installed or switched without an engineer. Similarly, other efficiency technologies apply to different aspects of fleet management. If 'Crew Coordination' is researched and the fleet has all required officers, components can be installed or switched without a shipyard, which is useful when isolated from space yards.

'Jump Drive Efficiency' reduces jump time, and the 'Black Hole Stabilizer' and 'Warp Gate Stabilizer' technologies enable travel through black holes and warp gates, respectively.

Currently, there are 12 technology branches and a total of 64 technologies, with more potentially being added in the future.

If you are interested in this project, please spread the word.

all the best,
Tensorial

notes.title: Stellar Insurgency Demo v3.0 is out
notes.content:
A [b]grid-based[/b] component system has been developed, allowing players to place components on a grid representing the spacecraft's hull.

Each component contributes either positive energy, like reactors, or negative energy, like engines. Players must strategically arrange components to maintain a positive overall energy net, or some may operate sub-optimally.

Damage to each cell is determined by the direction and impact point of incoming projectiles or laser bolts.

notes.title: Major Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone, happy New Year! Just wanted to say a big thanks for all your awesome support.

[b]Exciting developments are underway for Stellar Insurgency.[/b]

Over the past few months, I've dedicated myself to a significant upgrade, moving from the previous basic component system to a refined cell / grid-based design for ship components and implementing a damage system based on cells.

[h1][b]Overview[/b][/h1]

Each ship will boast a unique design, with the number of cells tailored to its size. For instance, capital ships will feature significantly more cells and a myriad of potential variations for component placement compared to smaller ships.

In this revamped system, reactors generate energy, while other ship components consume it. Every ship must possess one or more reactors to meet its energy requirements. Engines, vital for movement, find their place usually at the rear of the ship. Should the total energy consumption surpass the reactor's output, the ship's components will experience suboptimal functionality.  Moreover, designated positions on the ship will be available for turret placement. Turrets can be installed on either the upper or lower levels of the ship.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/34cd08e962948ff089e57758d7151c26e50ab790.png[/img]

Now, let's delve into the specific rules governing different weapon types.
[list]
[*] Energy Weapons primary damage order: Shield damage > Armor damage > Component damage
This aligns with the prevalent sci-fi concept where energy weapons prove effective against shields but exhibit diminishing effectiveness against armor and ship components.

[*] Missiles primary damage order: Armor damage > Component damage > Shields damage
Missiles, strategically effective against ship systems (components), introduce an additional layer of complexity. Their secondary impact on shields mirrors their explosive nature.

[*] Ballistic Weapons primary damage order: Component damage + Cell penetrating damage > Shields damage > Armor damage
Projectiles from ballistic weapons will have the ability to penetrate a ship's armor and inflict additional damage to its components.
[/list]

[h1][b]Individualized Damage[/b][/h1]

Damage to each component is now directly linked to both its location within the ship and the direction of the incoming projectile, energy bolt, or missile. Once a damage threshold is surpassed, the affected component will either sub-function or malfunction until it is replaced or repaired.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43647838/f1044f2c2a8d310dc9ecbc87c505afcc50fd1dce.png[/img]

[b]Please note that the demo does not feature the new component design system. However, this system will be included in the official alpha release, expected by the end of 2024.[/b]

Wishing you all the best,

Tensorial
